source_audit_support.citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule VII, Section 704

proposed.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VII, Section 704, two or more buildings on the same property may be treated as one building only if which condition is met?

options.text: All buildings share the same occupancy group and construction type, and abut one another along a common firewall
Their aggregate area does not exceed the allowable floor area for a single building, and the most restrictive occupancy and construction requirements are applied
They are located on separately titled lots that are consolidated by permit for the sole purpose of parking
They have identical heights and footprints, and each is provided with independent means of egress

proposed.rationale: Section 704 allows two or more buildings on the same property to be treated as one building only if their aggregate area is within the allowable floor area for a single building; where occupancy groups or construction types differ, the most restrictive requirements govern.
proposed.explanation: The assumed-property-line concept still applies to courts and walls facing another building; the consolidation rule is the exception and is constrained by the single-building area cap.
